text: The Science: Eating more potassium brings high blood pressure down (Aburto, et al, 2013), which matters on Strategy A, since its salts bring their own sodium. I think more potassium for the salt you eat helps the brain too: in one trial, a diet lower in salt and higher in potassium lifted mood a little (Torres, et al, 2008), though studies like it can't separate the potassium from the salt or the rest of the food. Stone Age diets are estimated to have had more than four times the potassium we eat now (Sebastian, et al, 2006), so eating closer to a paleo diet probably does more than adding a couple of potatoes, but the potatoes and greens below are the easy way to start. If you have kidney disease or take a blood pressure drug that holds on to potassium, like an ACE inhibitor or an ARB, ask your doctor first, since potassium can build up in your blood (NIH, 2022).
reader: someone with trauma or in withdrawal who is anxious, wired, numb or foggy, following the protocol's diet and electrolyte steps and wanting to know why each one is there

checked.point: low potassium (common in high stress) makes the KCNQ brakes fail, and eating potassium puts them back
checked.found: the brain keeps the potassium around its neurons within tight limits whatever the blood does (Hladky and Barrand 2016), so neither the drop stress brings to the blood (Brown 1983) nor what you eat sets the brakes
checked.still_needed: no: the brakes story is cut, with its two labels (blocks 104 and 105)

checked.point: eating more potassium brings high blood pressure down
checked.found: in trials, more potassium lowered systolic pressure by about 3.5 mm Hg, in people with high blood pressure and not in others (Aburto et al. 2013)
checked.still_needed: yes: they learn why the target and the foods that follow are there on Strategy A

checked.point: a higher potassium-to-sodium ratio helps the brain, mood included (his view)
checked.found: one small randomized trial: a low-sodium, high-potassium diet lifted mood a little, not separable from the salt or the food (Torres et al. 2008); memory and thinking mixed (Nowak et al. 2018, Zhao et al. 2025, Yoshida et al. 2026)
checked.still_needed: yes: they learn what the author thinks potassium does for the brain and how far the evidence goes

checked.point: Stone Age diets had far more potassium; a paleo diet probably does more than adding potatoes (his view)
checked.found: retrojected Stone Age diets: 400 +/- 125 mEq a day, more than four times current intakes (Sebastian et al. 2006); ten days of a paleo-type diet improved blood pressure and insulin in nine people (Frassetto et al. 2009)
checked.still_needed: yes: they can eat closer to a paleo diet as the fuller way, with the potatoes and greens as the start

checked.point: kidney disease and drugs that keep potassium in can let it build up
checked.found: ACE inhibitors and ARBs reduce urinary potassium excretion, which can lead to hyperkalemia (NIH 2022); in kidney disease, restricting potassium slowed neuropathy over two years (Arnold et al. 2017)
checked.still_needed: yes: they ask their doctor before eating more potassium if either applies to them
